correctness.rationale: A complete derivative proof shows a single Haldane inflection, then constructs a tangent quadratic contact and an exact nonnegative factorization with only two contact points. The piecewise response is a concave majorant, and Jensen inequality plus contact-set equality prove existence, global optimality, uniqueness, and boundary cases for every Borel law. Exact cleared-denominator rational identity and 11,188 deterministic standard-library checks passed. Tests are not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Primary full text gives the Haldane response and its inflection and fixes two levels when optimizing duty-cycle enhancement; it does not solve a fixed-mean, bounded arbitrary-law productivity maximum. An explicit globally supporting line, its radical lower contact, and a sharp loss identity classify all laws with unique equality. Related Beer–Lambert optical-depth work uses a constrained light distribution, not the present moment class. Generic concave-envelope principles are recognized as prior mathematics; risk of uninspected exact specialization remains.

value.rationale: The photoinhibitory Han/Haldane model motivates a natural finite-photon-budget and capped-illumination problem. The complete closed-form phase classification, constant lower setpoint above threshold, unique mixing weights and nonnegative performance-loss identity are operationally interpretable and do not follow from the cited fixed-pair duty-cycle theorem alone. The result is limited to equilibrium exposure mixtures; no unproved experimental benefits are claimed.
